items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: comfortable with me and with Jimmy Zitano, the drummer that I had recommended that they bring from Boston to play with her

ctx.x: It was a bit of a drag, like I have to ignore Aretha Franklin.

Sure, yeah. Well it was like that with Billie too. And I must have done well enough because she was certainly complimentary afterwards and comfortable with me and with Jimmy Zitano, the drummer that I had recommended that they bring from Boston to play with her, fine, fine drummer. We just spent a few minutes in the afternoon with Mal Waldron, the pianist, and went over a few things, and then bam we were onstage for the concert and, just as you described, if you don’t have a lot of room in your mind to pay…

I want to read something that came from your blog, and it has to do with that period of time I believe — I won’t read the whole thing but I found it quite interesting. “The musicians who grew up playing jazz in the U.S. in the 1940s and 50s had every reason to believe that they were pursuing their artistic activities in an atmosphere of common understanding with the members of the audience.
